evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Not asked. Joanna never asked the two-concerns opening question about movers showing up on time or damage to items.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised multiple concerns (freezer removal, storage rearrangement, grand piano, antique items) but Joanna acknowledged each with minimal follow-up and moved to next topic rather than probing two layers deep. Example: Customer mentions water leak damage to boxes; Joanna says 'I see, mm-hmm' and pivots to storage questions without asking tell-me-more.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Joanna offered value days framing: 'Sundays to Thursdays are our best value days. So that's lower compared to a Friday or a Saturday' and gave the dollar difference ($96 vs $103 per hour per mover, $7 difference). She asked about availability but did not isolate a specific cheaper day for this customer or ask flexibility directly; the discussion was general rate structure.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Never asked. Joanna provided pricing estimates ($2964 for pack/move, $2500 for storage, ~$5-6k total) and email follow-up promise but never mentioned rate lock, no-deposit guarantee, or asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' The call ended with customer saying 'I'll get started with pictures' and no explicit booking ask.

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details (address, square footage, stories, rooms, oversized items, parking, special items like antique furniture and grandfather clock) and identified key constraints early, building a nuanced picture of a complex multi-part move.
coaching_note: You skipped the two-concerns question entirely and never asked for the business at the end of the call—these are the two bookends of the card that matter most to customers; go back and embed both into your rhythm.
